statements.claim: Muchukunda woke to find a heap of ashes at the cave's mouth, where the one who had pursued Krishna into the mountain had been consumed by his own wickedness.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.21 ('yavane bhasma-sān nīte') and 10.51.32 ('so 'pi bhasmī-kṛto nūnam ātmīyenaiva pāpmanā' - reduced to ashes by his own sin); pursuit context from corpus chain (DKS_0174).

statements.claim: Before him stood a young man dark as a laden rain cloud, dressed in yellow silk, four-armed, radiant, wearing a garland of forest flowers (Vaijayanti), with a smile of pure affection.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.22-24: ghana-śyāmaṃ pīta-kauśeya-vāsasam, catur-bhujaṃ rocamānaṃ, vaijayantyā mālayā, sānurāga-smitekṣaṇam.

statements.claim: Muchukunda, senses worn by his long vigil, asked whether he was the fire/lord of fire, the best of the three lords of the worlds, whose splendor he could not bear to look upon.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.25-33: cira-prajāgara-śrānto nidrayāpahatendriyaḥ; 'kiṃ svit tejasvināṃ tejo... vibhāvasuḥ'; 'trayāṇāṃ puruṣarṣabham'; 'tejasā te 'viṣahyeṇa... draṣṭuṃ na śaknumaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna said he had measured the dust of the earth through many births and known the deeds of all three times; Kalanemi, Kamsa, Pralamba and other haters of the good had been slain for the relief of the world; and he had entered the cave for Muchukunda's sake, offering any boon.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.36-42: rajāṃsi vimame... uru-janmabhiḥ; kāla-trayopapannāni; kālanemir hataḥ kaṃsaḥ pralambādyāś ca sad-dviṣaḥ; so 'haṃ tavānugrahārthaṃ guhām etām upāgataḥ; varān vṛṇīṣva.

statements.claim: Muchukunda reflected that he had once conquered the circle of the directions and sat on an excellent throne honored by kings, and that the king's body is only a jar of clay that ends as ordure, worms and ashes.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.47-50: kalevare ghaṭa-kuḍya-sannibhe; kalevaro viṭ-kṛmi-bhasma-saṃjñitaḥ; nirjitya dik-cakram... varāsana-sthaḥ sama-rāja-vanditaḥ.

statements.claim: Muchukunda declared he desired no boon but the service of Krishna's feet, counting the kingdom's falling away as Krishna's grace, renouncing all blessing that binds, and asking only for refuge.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.52-56: sat-samāgamaḥ; rājyānubandhāpagamo yadṛcchayā; na kāmaye 'nyaṃ tava pāda-sevanād... varaṃ; visṛjyāśiṣaḥ... guṇānubandhanāḥ; abhayam ṛtam aśokaṃ pāhi.

statements.claim: Krishna answered that Muchukunda's not being tempted by the boons was his true wakefulness, that the undisciplined devotion of breath and mind does not reach him, that he should wander the earth with his mind fixed on Krishna; and that in his next birth he would be born a brahmana, friend of all beings, and attain Krishna alone.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.58-62 (apramādāya; prāṇāyāmādibhiḥ; vicarasva mahīṃ... mayy āveśita-mānasaḥ; janmany anantare... sarva-bhūta-suhṛttamaḥ); brahmana rebirth + attaining him alone per pack index summary of 10.51.21-62.

statements.claim: Muchukunda rose from the cave floor and walked out a wanderer; the long sleep of the king of the Ikshvakus was over.
statements.evidence: BP 10.51.60 (wander the earth) and 10.51.30 (aikṣvākāḥ); closing connective framing consistent with the grant.

notes: Faithful rendering of BP 10.51.21-62. 'Young man' and 'golden throne' are minor ornamental details; no unsupported or contradicted factual claims found.

statements.claim: Jarasandha marched on Mathura again with an immense army, unable to forgive that the city sheltered the two brothers and had turned him back before.
statements.evidence: BP 10.52.1-13 pursuit episode; prior repeated defeats per arc (BP 10.70.29: broken eighteen times; corpus chain of Jarasandha sieges).

statements.claim: Krishna had already sent the city's wealth - herds and treasure - away with men he had chosen.
statements.evidence: BP 10.52.5: nīyamāne dhane gobhir nṛbhiś cācyuta-coditaiḥ (wealth carried away with cows and men at Acyuta's command).

statements.claim: Seeing the enemy's rush, Krishna and Balarama abandoned the abundant wealth and fled on foot as if terrified.
statements.evidence: BP 10.52.6-8: vihāya vittaṃ pracuram abhītau bhīru-bhīta-vat; palāyamānau tau dṛṣṭvā māgadhaḥ prahasan balī.

statements.claim: Exhausted, they climbed Mt. Pravarshana and hid among its rocks and trees; Jarasandha's men found no trace of them, and the king set the mountain on fire.
statements.evidence: BP 10.52.9-11: śrāntau tuṅgam āruhatāṃ girim; girau nilīnāv... nādhigamya padam; dahyamāna-taṭāt; mountain and fire-setter per pack summary.

statements.claim: From the burning slope the brothers leapt eleven yojanas, unseen by Jarasandha and his followers, and returned to their sea-girt city.
statements.evidence: BP 10.52.11-12: utpatya tarasā dahyamāna-taṭād ubhau; alakṣyamāṇau ripuṇā sānugena; 'eleven yojanas' and 'sea-girt city' per pack summary.

statements.claim: Jarasandha returned believing the brothers had burned in his fire and told the story of their destruction, satisfied with a false victory.
statements.evidence: BP 10.52.13: so 'pi dagdhāv iti mṛṣā manvāno bala-keśavau.

statements.claim: The whole pursuit - the flight, the hill, the fire - had been shaped deliberately: the brothers chose to be thought dead so Jarasandha would stop pursuing.
statements.evidence: Index summary 'feign flight from Jarasandha'; BP 10.52.7 bhīru-bhīta-vat (like men afraid) supports the feigned character of the flight.

statements.claim: Jarasandha told his generals that this time there would be no third campaign.
statements.evidence: Character bravado/dialogue; no sourceable campaign count in the pack (canonical 'eighteen times' defeats belong to the arc, BP 10.70.29).

notes: Solid rendering of BP 10.52.1-13; 'no third campaign' is rhetorical villain dialogue, not a sourced count - noted but not treated as a factual error.

statements.claim: In Krishna's assembly at Dwaraka, with brahmanas seated, a man of unprecedented appearance was admitted and bowed to Krishna with joined palms.
statements.evidence: BP 10.70.20-22: brāhmaṇāḥ... āsīnā brahma-vādinaḥ; puruṣo 'pūrva-darśanaḥ; namaskṛtya kṛṣṇāya... kṛtāñjaliḥ.

statements.claim: The man reported that Jarasandha had forcibly imprisoned the kings who refused to submit during his conquest of the directions - twenty thousand of them - in his fortress at Girivraja.
statements.evidence: BP 10.70.23 (ye ca dig-vijaye tasya sannatiṃ na yayur nṛpāḥ); 'twenty thousand of them in Girivraja' per pack summary of 10.70.20-30.

statements.claim: The captive kings' message: the strong cut short the weak's hopes in this world; a king's happiness is only a dream depending on others, carried in bodies ever afraid; they take refuge in Krishna from the terror of the world, and his feet remove the sorrow of those who bow - free them from the bond of Magadha, where Jarasandha holds them with the strength of ten thousand elephants, like a lion penning sheep.
statements.evidence: BP 10.70.25-28: balavān... jīvitāśāṃ sadyaś chinatti; svapnāyitaṃ nṛpa-sukhaṃ para-tantram; śaśvad-bhayena mṛtakena dhuraṃ vahāmaḥ; praṇata-śoka-harāṅghri-yugmo; baddhān viyuṅkṣva magadhāhvaya-karma-pāśāt; ayuta-mataṅgaja-vīryam; mṛga-rāḍ ivāvīḥ.

statements.claim: The kings reminded Krishna that Jarasandha had been broken eighteen times in battle by Krishna with his discus raised, and yet still swells with pride and oppresses Krishna's people.
statements.evidence: BP 10.70.29: dvi-nava-kṛtva udātta-cakra bhagno mṛdhe... ūḍha-darpo... yuṣmat-prajā rujati.

statements.claim: The kings said Krishna descended into the world for the protection of the good and the restraint of the wicked, and asked him to ordain an end to it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.70.26: sad-rakṣaṇāya khala-nigrahaṇāya kalayāvatīrṇaḥ; tad vidhehi (10.70.29).

statements.claim: The messenger's words left the assembly still; twenty thousand prisoners hung on Krishna's answer.
statements.evidence: Closing scene-setting; the messenger's relay (dūta uvāca at 10.70.30) frames the speech as delivered at court.

notes: Accurate to BP 10.70.20-30; the speech is correctly framed as the messenger relaying the captive kings' words (dūta uvāca). No issues.

statements.claim: Uddhava counselled that the Rajasuya is the imperial rite to be performed by one who has conquered the circle of the directions, and that Jarasandha, who holds twenty thousand kings at Girivraja, stands across that path.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.2: yaṣṭavyam rājasūyena dik-cakra-jayinā; captivity of the kings per BP 10.70 (corpus chain); plan framed in Uddhava's voice per variant note (BP attribution).

statements.claim: One deed serves two ends: bring Jarasandha down and the directions lie open for the sacrifice and the captive kings go free.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.3 (asmākaṃ ca mahān artho hy etenaiva bhaviṣyati) and 10.71.9 (jarāsandha-vadhaḥ kṛṣṇa bhūry-arthāyopakalpate); pack summary: 'defeating Jarasandha serves both purposes'.

statements.claim: Jarasandha's strength equals ten thousand elephants, and he cannot be conquered even with a hundred akṣauhiṇīs.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.4-5: nāgāyuta-samo bale; mā śatākṣauhiṇī-yutaḥ.

statements.claim: He could only be met in single combat - a duel of two chariots - and the one man who could match him was Bhima.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.5-6: dvai-rathe sa tu jetavyaḥ; brahma-veṣa-dharo gatvā taṃ bhikṣeta vṛkodaraḥ.

statements.claim: Bhima would go to Girivraja disguised as a brahmana and beg for the duel, and Jarasandha - proud of his strength - would grant it, to be slain before Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.6; pack summary ('request single combat, and slay him before Krishna'); Jarasandha's pride granting the challenge consistent with 10.72.29-31 outcome.

statements.claim: The women of the captive courts, the gopis, the daughter of Janaka, and the sages who found refuge in Krishna sing of the enemy's fall and their release; all who look to Krishna await this deed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.8: gāyanti te viśada-karma gṛheṣu devyo rājñāṃ sva-śatru-vadham ātma-vimokṣaṇaṃ ca; gopyaś ca... janakātmajāyāḥ... munayo vayaṃ ca.

statements.claim: Krishna accepted the plan: Bhima in a brahmana's guise, Krishna and Arjuna there to see it through, the quarrel ending on a field of single combat.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.6 plan + 10.72.15 execution (bhīmaseno 'rjunaḥ kṛṣṇo brahma-linga-dharās trayaḥ jagmur girivrajaṃ), per corpus chain.

notes: Matches BP 10.71.1-10. 'One direction that never bowed' is a rhetorical gloss on Jarasandha's unconquered status; no issues.

statements.claim: Yudhishthira was preparing the Rajasuya and Krishna departed Dwaraka for Indraprastha, entrusting the city to Balarama and mounting his Garuda-bannered chariot.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.11-13 (athādiśat prayāṇāya; Garuda banner and Balarama per pack summary); Rajasuya purpose per 10.71.1-10 and 10.72.1-15 (corpus chain).

statements.claim: He set out surrounded by an immense army - chariots, horsemen, elephants, foot soldiers - while mridangas, bheris, the deep anaka, conches and gomukha horns resounded.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.13: ratha-dvipa-bhaṭa... mṛdaṅga-bhery-ānaka-śaṅkha-gomukhaiḥ praghoṣa-ghoṣita-kakubho nirakramat; 10.71.16 (army with banners, weapons, armor).

statements.claim: Behind the army came the women of the palace - Krishna's wives with their children and attendants - in gilded palanquins, followed by trains of oxen, camels, mules, asses, buffaloes and she-elephants carrying household goods.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.12 (sva-varodhān sa-sutān sa-paricchadān), 10.71.14 (nṛ-vāji-kāñcana-śibikābhir... sahātmajāḥ patim anu), 10.71.15 (naroṣṭra-go-mahiṣa-kharāśvatary-anaḥ kareṇubhiḥ parijana-vāra-yoṣitaḥ).

statements.claim: The sage Narada met them, was honored by Krishna, bowed, and rose through the sky carrying Krishna in his heart.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.17: munir yadu-patinā sabhājitaḥ praṇamya taṃ hṛdi vidadhad vihāyasā.

statements.claim: Krishna sent a royal messenger ahead to the kings whose lands the road crossed, so that no ruler would mistake the army for an invasion.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.18-19: rāja-dūtam uvācedaṃ bhagavān prīṇayan girā; ity uktaḥ prasthito dūto yathā-vad avadan nṛpān (the courtesy/signal reading is a fair gloss on the messenger's mission).

statements.claim: The route ran through Anarta, the dry country of Sauvira, the wastes of Maru, and Vinashana, then crossed the Drishadvati and the Sarasvati.
statements.evidence: BP 10.71.20-21: ānarta-sauvīra-marūṃs tīrtvā vinaśanaṃ hariḥ; tato dṛṣadvatīṃ tīrtvā... sarasvatīm.

statements.claim: Everywhere they passed, towns emptied into the streets and local kings rode out to greet Krishna and ride part of the way with him.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere consistent with the herald's advance notice (10.71.19) but not detailed in the verses.

notes: Faithful to BP 10.71.11-21 including the exact route names. Departure purpose (Rajasuya summons) is supported by the surrounding 10.70-10.72 context in the corpus chain.

statements.claim: Bhima slew Jarasandha in single combat outside the city, in a duel long enough to shatter two great maces.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.32-43: Jarasandha took a second mace and went out of the city (nirjagāma purād bahiḥ); the two maces were pulverized (gade... cūrṇī-babhūvatuḥ) before Bhima split him (10.72.40-43).

statements.claim: Krishna installed Jarasandha's son Sahadeva as lord of the Magadhas before the assembled court and elders.
statements.evidence: Pack summary of BP 10.72.45: 'Krishna installs Jarasandha's son Sahadeva as lord of the Magadhas'.

statements.claim: Krishna released the kings Jarasandha had held captive in Girivraja, who came out into the light after long captivity.
statements.evidence: Pack summary of BP 10.72.45: 'releases the kings who had been held captive by Jarasandha'; the story's note that the old text gives the release a single line matches the single-verse citation.

statements.claim: Jarasandha had not held the kings for ransom but had gathered them with the intent of offering them as a sacrifice to Rudra.
statements.evidence: MBh 2.22 (carried in corpus chain pack DKS_0182): Krishna charges Jarasandha with bringing the Kshatriyas of the world as captives 'to offer them as sacrifice unto the god Rudra'; captivity itself per BP 10.70.23-28. (The BP-only excerpt of 10.72.45 shows imprisonment and release without the motive, which the MBh source in the same arc supplies.)

statements.claim: The kingdom of Magadha was handed back to its own line - a son of Jarasandha's on the throne - rather than destroyed, and the kings were freed with no conditions asked.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.45 (installation of the son + release of the kings as one act); no conditions appear in the source; closing interpretation consistent with it.

statements.claim: With Jarasandha dead and the kings freed, the last obstacle on the road to the Rajasuya was gone.
statements.evidence: Arc: the Rajasuya plan required conquering the directions (BP 10.71.1-10) and proceeds thereafter in the corpus chain.

notes: The Rudra-sacrifice motive is sourced from MBh 2.22 (same arc, pack DKS_0182) rather than the BP 10.72.45 excerpt alone - noted for the record; both sources are part of this corpus's evidence set for the episode.

statements.claim: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna, disguised as brahmanas, went to Girivraja and presented themselves at Jarasandha's house at the hour of hospitality, asking alms as suppliants from afar.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.15-17: brahma-linga-dharās trayaḥ jagmur girivrajaṃ; atithya-velāyāṃ gṛheṣu; rājan viddhy atithīn prāptān arthino dūram āgatān; MBh 2.20 (garb of Snataka Brahmanas).

statements.claim: They came on a plan Krishna had argued and Yudhishthira had accepted: Jarasandha, unbeatable in open battle even by all the celestials, could be vanquished only in personal combat.
statements.evidence: MBh 2.20 (in this pack): Krishna's speech to Yudhishthira and Yudhishthira's assent; 'incapable of being vanquished in battle even by all the celestials and the Asuras... should be vanquished in a personal struggle with bare arms'.

statements.claim: The road was long: from the country of the Kurus through Kuru-jangala, past the lake of lotuses and the hills of Kalakuta, across the Gandaki and the Sarayu, through the eastern lands and past Mithila, then across the Ganges and the Sone, until the hills of Goratha rose before the city of Magadha, filled with cattle and grain and water.
statements.evidence: MBh 2.20 (quoted in pack): 'set out from the country of the Kurus, passed through Kuru-jangala... lake of lotuses... hills of Kalakuta... crossing the Gandaki... Sarayu... Eastern Kosala... Mithila... crossed the Ganges and the Sone... hills of Goratha, they saw the city of Magadha... filled with kine and wealth and water.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha was a king famed for giving, of whom it was said he would part with anything a guest asked, even his own head.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.26: dadāmy ātma-śiro 'pi vaḥ; pack summary: 'the generous king, famed for giving even his own head to suppliants'.

statements.claim: Studying their voices, bearing and the marks on their arms, Jarasandha recognized these as royal men wearing a brahmana's guise.
statements.evidence: Pack summary of BP 10.72.14-26: 'recognizing them by their voices and marks'; BP 10.72.22: rājanya-bandhavo hy ete brahma-liṅgāni bibhrati; bowstring scars are the warrior mark read from 'marks'.

statements.claim: He reflected on Bali - who gave the earth to Vishnu in a dwarf brahmana's guise and lost his kingdom but kept his fame - and on Harishchandra, Rantideva, Shibi, a hunter and a pigeon, who won eternal honor with perishable bodies by giving.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.19-20, 23-24: hariścandro rantideva uñchavṛttiḥ śibir baliḥ; vyādhaḥ kapoto bahavo hy adhruveṇa dhruvaṃ gatāḥ; baler... kīrtir... vipra-vyājena viṣṇunā; dvija-rūpiṇe... mahīm prādād.

statements.claim: His answer was large: choose whatever you desire, and I will give it - even my very head.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.26: ity udāra-matiḥ prāha kṛṣṇārjuna-vṛkodarān; he viprā vriyatāṃ kāmo dadāmy ātma-śiro 'pi vaḥ.

notes: Excellent fidelity: route details match MBh 2.20 nearly verbatim; generosity exemplars and the 'even my head' promise match BP 10.72. No issues.

statements.claim: Krishna asked for battle - single combat, man to man - declaring they were warriors who had come desiring war, then named Bhima (Vrikodara, son of Pandu), his brother Arjuna, and himself Krishna, their cousin and Jarasandha's enemy.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.27-28: yuddhaṃ no dehi rājendra dvandvaśo... rājanyā nānya-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ; asau vṛkodaraḥ pārthas tasya bhrātārjuno hy ayam; anayor mātuleyaṃ māṃ kṛṣṇaṃ jānīhi te ripum; MBh 2.22: 'I am Hrishesha otherwise called Sauri, and these two heroes... sons of Pandu'.

statements.claim: Krishna charged Jarasandha with bringing the Kshatriyas of the world here as captives to offer in sacrifice to Rudra - human slaughter never seen among the virtuous - and bade him set the kings free or go to the abode of Yama.
statements.evidence: MBh 2.22 (in pack): 'Thou hast brought... many of the Kshatriyas of the world as captives... seekest to offer them as sacrifice unto the god Rudra!... The slaughter of human being as sacrifice unto the gods is never seen... Either set free all the monarchs, or go thou to the abode of Yama.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha laughed aloud and answered that he could not recollect ever having wronged the three, and that he never made a captive of a king not first vanquished in fair war - every man in his prison had been beaten in battle, the law of his order being to bring others under sway by prowess.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.29 (jahāsoccaiḥ); MBh 2.22: 'I do not recollect if I ever acted injuriously towards ye... I never make a captive of a king without first vanquishing him... bring others under sway by the exhibition of prowess and then to treat them as slaves.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha refused to fight Krishna, taunting him as a coward who had abandoned his own city of Mathura and fled to the sea.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.30: na tvayā bhīruṇā yotsye... mathurāṃ sva-purīṃ tyaktvā samudraṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ.

statements.claim: He judged Arjuna no match, but Bhima his equal in age and strength - the fight he wanted - so he gave Bhima a great mace, took a second for himself, and walked out through the city gates to the level ground outside the walls.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.31-33: ayaṃ tu vayasātulyo... arjuno na bhaved yoddhā bhīmas tulya-balo mama; ity uktvā bhīmasenāya prādāya mahatīṃ gadām dvitīyāṃ svayam ādāya nirjagāma purād bahiḥ; samekhale (level arena) at 10.72.33.

statements.claim: Bhima followed him out, with Krishna and Arjuna behind, as the city of Girivraja gathered to see the strongest man of Magadha meet his challenger.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.32-33 (the duel is joined in public on the level ground outside the city); crowd-gathering is connective framing consistent with a public duel before witnesses.

notes: Blends BP 10.72.27-32 and MBh 2.22 accurately; the two sources' elements (BP's short reveal/laugh/taunt, MBh's fuller accusation and defense) are combined without contradiction. No issues.
